'''Tatiana Toro''' (born 1964) is a Colombian-American mathematician at the [[University of Washington]].<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://www.math.washington.edu/~toro/web-cv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Tatiana Toro|access-date=2015-10-06}}.</ref> Her research is "at the interface of [[geometric measure theory]], [[harmonic analysis]] and [[partial differential equation]]s".<ref name="gug">{{citation|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/tatiana-toro/|title=Guggenheim fellows: Tatiana Toro|publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|access-date=2015-10-06|archive-date=2019-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191016001210/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/tatiana-toro/|url-status=dead}}.</ref> Toro was appointed director of the [[Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute]] for 2022–2027.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-07-12|website=www.msri.org}}</ref>

== Education and employment ==
Toro was born in 1964 in [[Colombia]],<ref name="gug" /><ref name=slmath>{{cite news |url=https://www.elespectador.com/ciencia/tatiana-toro-una-colombiana-es-nombrada-directora-del-instituto-de-investigaciones-en-ciencias-matematicas-de-eeuu/ |title=Tatiana Toro, the Colombian appointed director of the US Mathematical Sciences Research Institute. |date=2021-06-15 |work=[[El Espectador]] |language=es}}</ref> and attended the [[Lycée français Louis Pasteur (Colombia)|Lycée Français Louis Pasteur]] in [[Bogotá]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.mathvalues.org/masterblog/testimonios-dr-tatiana-toro |title=Testimonios: Dr. Tatiana Toro |date=2023-07-15 |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]}}</ref> She competed for Colombia in the 1981 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=16643|title=Tatiana Toro|publisher=[[International Mathematical Olympiad]]|access-date=2015-10-06}}.</ref> and earned a bachelor's degree from the [[National University of Colombia]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/tatiana-toro|title=Tatiana Toro|publisher=Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study, Harvard University|access-date=2015-10-06}}.</ref> In 1992, she was awarded her PhD at [[Stanford University]], under the supervision of [[Leon Simon]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=39263}}</ref> After short-term positions at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[University of California, Berkeley]], and [[University of Chicago]], she joined the University of Washington faculty in 1996.<ref name="cv" /> Since August 2022, Toro serves as the director of [[Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute]] (formerly MSRI).<ref name=slmath /> She will maintain her tenure at the University of Washington throughout her term.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-15|website=www.msri.org}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Toro was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=2015-10-06|archive-date=2017-11-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref> She became a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] in 2015.<ref name="gug" /> She was elected as a member of the 2017 class of [[Fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to geometric measure theory, [[potential theory]], and free boundary theory".<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2017 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], [[American Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2016-11-06.</ref> At the University of Washington, she was the Robert R. & Elaine F. Phelps Professor in Mathematics from 2012 to 2016<ref>[https://www.math.washington.edu/Research/fac-awards.php Recent faculty awards], University of Washington, retrieved 2016-11-06.</ref> and is currently the Craig McKibben and Sarah Merner Professor. Toro was named [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Chancellor's Professor for 2016–17.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-07|website=www.msri.org}}</ref> She was awarded the 2020 [[Blackwell-Tapia Prize]].<ref>{{citation|title=The Latest|url=http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6217|access-date=2020-07-21|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en}}</ref> She was elected fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences|American Academy of Arts and Sciences (AAAS)]] in 2020.<ref>{{citation|title=AAAS Fellows Elected|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202007/rnoti-p1051.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society}}</ref> Toro was awarded the  [[ICMAM Prize]] 2022 of the research organization ICMAM Latin America.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/view/icmamlatinamerica/icmam-prize |title=ICMAM Latin America - ICMAM Prize }}</ref>  Toro was honored as the [[AWM/MAA Falconer Lecturer]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-07 |title=AWM-MAA Etta Zuber Falconer Lecturer Announced |url=https://awm-math.org/awm-maa-etta-zuber-falconer-lecturer-announced/ |access-date=2023-03-15 |website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) |language=en-US}}</ref>
